title: Titrations and solution calculations; Limiting reagent and yield
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AM09#t2 term and clue written for the game; AM09#t3 term and clue written for the game; AM09#t1 term and clue written for the game; AM09#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM08b#N.3, AM09#N.4a, AM08b#N.5, AM09#N.6, AM08b#N.10, AM09#N.10b.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Excess reactant
items.clue: The starting substance of which some is left over at the end.

items.label: Theoretical yield
items.clue: The maximum mass of product, calculated from the substance that runs out first.

items.label: Limiting reactant
items.clue: The starting substance used up first, which fixes the maximum quantity of product.

items.label: Actual yield
items.clue: The mass of product obtained in practice, normally less than the calculated maximum.

questions.stem: In a back titration, an insoluble carbonate is added to excess hydrochloric acid, and the leftover acid is titrated with sodium hydroxide. Which amount equals the moles of HCl that reacted with the carbonate?

options.text: The moles of NaOH used in the titration of the leftover acid
The moles of HCl added to the solid at the very start
The moles of HCl added minus the moles of NaOH used in the titre
Half the moles of NaOH used in the titration of the leftover acid

questions.explanation: HCl reacts 1 : 1 with NaOH, so n(NaOH) = acid left over. Subtract it from the acid added to get the acid the carbonate used.

questions.stem: Nitrogen and hydrogen react: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g). A mixture contains 5.60 g of N₂ and 1.50 g of H₂. Which statement is correct? (Aᵣ: H 1.0, N 14.0)

options.text: H₂ is limiting, because a smaller mass of H₂ is present.
H₂ is limiting, because the equation needs three times as much H₂ as N₂.
H₂ is limiting: 0.750 mol H₂ needs 2.25 mol N₂, and only 0.200 mol N₂ is present.
N₂ is limiting: 0.200 mol N₂ needs 0.600 mol H₂, and 0.750 mol H₂ is present.

questions.explanation: n(N₂) = 5.60 ÷ 28.0 = 0.200 mol; n(H₂) = 1.50 ÷ 2.0 = 0.750 mol. N₂ needs 3 × 0.200 = 0.600 mol H₂, which is available, so N₂ runs out first.

questions.stem: 10.0 cm³ of vinegar is diluted to 100.0 cm³ in a volumetric flask. A 25.0 cm³ portion needs 20.75 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH. CH₃COOH + NaOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O. What was the concentration of ethanoic acid in the original vinegar, in mol dm⁻³?
questions.explanation: n(NaOH) = 0.100 × 0.02075 = 2.075 × 10⁻³ mol = n(acid) in the portion. 2.075 × 10⁻³ ÷ 0.0250 = 0.0830 diluted; × 10 = 0.830 in the vinegar.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the theoretical yield of a product in a reaction?

options.text: The mass of product actually obtained at the end of the experiment
The total mass of all the reactants put in, since mass is conserved
The mass of product calculated from the amount of the limiting reactant
The mass of product calculated from the reactant with the smaller number of moles

questions.explanation: The theoretical yield is the maximum mass of product, from the limiting reactant and the mole ratio, assuming complete reaction and no losses.

questions.stem: An impure sample of magnesium oxide, an insoluble base, is analysed by back titration. MgO(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl₂(aq) + H₂O(l). Assume the impurities do not react with acid. 0.400 g of the sample is added to 25.0 cm³ of 1.00 mol dm⁻³ HCl (excess). The leftover acid needs 14.30 cm³ of 0.500 mol dm⁻³ NaOH. What is the percentage by mass of MgO in the sample? (Aᵣ: O 16.0, Mg 24.3)

Thermite is a mixture of aluminium and iron(III) oxide. 2Al(s) + Fe₂O₃(s) → Al₂O₃(s) + 2Fe(l). A mixture of 10.0 g of Al and 10.0 g of Fe₂O₃ reacts, and 5.60 g of iron is collected. What is the percentage yield of iron? (Molar masses: Al 27.0, Fe₂O₃ 159.6, Fe 55.8 g mol⁻¹)
questions.explanation: n(Al) = 0.370 mol; n(Fe₂O₃) = 0.0627 mol. Divided by coefficients, 0.185 against 0.0627: Fe₂O₃ limits. n(Fe) = 2 × 0.0627 = 0.125 mol; theoretical 6.99 g. 5.60 ÷ 6.99 × 100 = 80.1%.
